contexts.text: As the day grew warm () = from love. Explained.
All affection is signified by warmth, even in common discourse.
To grow warm () is predicated of evil.
The flocks grew warm at the rods () = the effect from His Own power; for to grow warm = the effect of the affection.
To grow warm = the ardour and effect of affection; (and therefore it = ) the things which are spontaneous. Explained. AC 4031.
That it might grow warm () = that they might be conjoined. AC 4082.
To grow warm with gods () = with concupiscences of what is false. ( = the ardour of worship. AC 10137:7.)
The sun grew warm, and it melted () = that (the good of truth) vanishes according to the degree of increasing concupiscence. Explained.
When in externals, man... grows warm from the world, and grows cold to Heaven.

That love is heat from a spiritual origin, is evident from man's warmth according to love; for man is kindled and grows warm according to the quantity and quality of it... HH 567. DLW 95. DLW 379:2. CL 380:12.
As to the interiors of their minds, men grow warm from that Sun.
Hence it is said... that they grow warm with God.
That it may grow warm from an illicit fire.
To inflame one's self with gods under every green tree () = to worship God from every falsity that occurs; to inflame one's self with gods = ardent worship.
The ardour of those who unite in doing this, is signified by, when they are heated I will set their feasts ().
